en: Dependent on a state with resistance (*sappaṭigha*), a state without resistance (*nasappaṭigha*) arises by way of the root condition (*hetupaccaya*).
Dependent on a state with resistance, a state that is not without resistance (*naappaṭigha*) arises by way of the root condition.
Dependent on a state with resistance, states that are both without resistance and not without resistance arise by way of the root condition.
Dependent on a non-reactive (appaṭigha) state, a non-non-reactive (naappaṭigha) state arises by way of the root condition (hetupaccaya).
Dependent on a non-reactive state, a non-non-reactive state arises by way of the root condition.
Dependent on a non-reactive state, both non-non-reactive and non-reactive states arise by way of the root condition.
Dependent on both impinging and non-impinging phenomena, a non-impinging phenomenon arises by way of the root condition.
Dependent on both impinging and non-impinging phenomena, a non-non-impinging phenomenon arises by way of the root condition.
Dependent on both impinging and non-impinging phenomena, both non-impinging and non-non-impinging phenomena arise.
They arise by way of the root condition. (Abbreviated.
Nine in the case of the root; one in the case of the object … pe … six in the case of mutuality … pe … nine in the case of non-disappearance. (The full detail applies everywhere.)
